motion.name: pendulum
motion.value: a" = -k(a - rest) - d·a'  with k = 2600/L and d = 1.35 + min(L,260)/460
motion.purpose: Every hanging tag. Stiffness falls with cord length, so a long tag swings slower than a short one and the wall never moves in unison.

motion.name: pointer
motion.purpose: The cursor is a force, not a trigger. Nearer and lighter tags move further.

motion.name: scroll
motion.purpose: Scrolling knocks the whole rail at once.

motion.name: clamp
motion.purpose: Past 13 degrees a tag stops being readable; the limit bleeds the swing rather than stopping it dead.

motion.name: sleep
motion.value: park below 0.02deg and 0.02deg/s, wake on disturbance
motion.purpose: An idle page must cost nothing. The loop stops roughly 8s after load.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: The only conventional reveal on the page, used below the fold where physics has nothing to act on.

components.name: Hanging Tag
components.description: The system's atom: a hook, a cord, and a punched bone face. transform-origin sits at the hook so rotation swings cord and face together.
components.css: .ds-tag { position: absolute; top: 0; left: var(--x); width: var(--w); margin-left: calc(var(--w) / -2); transform-origin: 50% 0; transform: rotate(var(--tilt)); display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; will-change: transform; } .ds-hook { width: 13px; height: 13px; border: 2px solid #C9A227; border-radius: 50%; margin-top: -6px; } .ds-cord { width: 2px; height: var(--drop); background: linear-gradient(#C9A227, #7A6116); } .ds-face { position: relative; width: 100%; background: #EDE7D9; color: #14211F; border-radius: 3px; padding: 1.5rem .75rem .7rem; text-align: center; box-shadow: 0 14px 30px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.85), 0 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.25); } .ds-face::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: .5rem; left: 50%; translate: -50% 0; width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: #081F23; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.6); } .ds-face b { display: block; font: 800 1.0625rem/1 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.03em; } .ds-face i { font-style: normal; font-size: .6875rem; color: #4A5A56; }

narrative.overview: The surface is the key rack Justin worked behind for eight years, turned into the index of what he is opening next. The compartments do not hold hotel rooms; they hold his next moves. That inversion is the whole system: hospitality is where the authority came from, never the identity, so the page can lean hard on the operating record without trapping him inside it. Everything descends from one physical fact — a tag hangs, and a hanging thing swings. The first viewport is a brass rail carrying seven bone tags, each a damped pendulum with its own natural frequency, and the visitor's cursor is a force applied to them. Nothing fades up on scroll. The rendering is graphic rather than skeuomorphic: no imitation brass, no bevels, no embossing, because those are the tells of a machine imitating a material it cannot render. Depth comes from two honest sources only — real cast shadow and real motion.
keyCharacteristics: A tag hangs, and a hanging thing swings — every other decision descends from that
The cursor is a force applied to a simulation, not a trigger that plays a timeline
Graphic, never skeuomorphic: depth is shadow and motion, never imitation material
Compartments are recesses with inset shadow, explicitly not cards
Bone is a material for objects; the petrol field owns the page

rules.name: Everything That Hangs Is A Tag
rules.body: A hook, a cord of --drop height, a punched bone face, and transform-origin at the hook. Any new hanging element uses this atom and takes --x, --drop, --w and --tilt.

rules.name: Bone Is An Object
rules.body: Bone appears only where something is physically a card in this world — a tag face, the register page. Never a section ground. The field owns the page and bone objects sit on it.

rules.name: Brass Is Structure, Oxblood Is State
rules.body: Brass elements are part of the rack: rail, hook, cord, key number, the primary action. Oxblood elements are statuses. Never swap them.

rules.name: Readability Outranks The Toy
rules.body: Swing is clamped to ±13 degrees off rest. Past that a tag stops being readable, and the limit bleeds velocity rather than stopping it dead.

rules.name: The Loop Must Sleep
rules.body: Physics parks when every tag is within 0.02 degrees of rest and wakes on the next disturbance. An idle page costs nothing; a simulation that runs forever is a battery bug.

rules.name: Restage, Don't Shrink
rules.body: Below 48em four tags are hidden and the remaining three stack vertically rather than scaling down. Seven scaled tags on a phone is a collision, not a layout.

rules.name: Two Directions Of Tracking
rules.body: Bricolage tightens as it grows (to -0.045em); Familjen labels widen (to 0.18em). The opposing directions are what keep one voice from blurring into the other.

dos: Do hang anything that can hang
Do keep bone for objects only; the field owns the page
Do use brass for structure and oxblood for state
Do clamp the swing and let the loop sleep
Do draw hooks and holes as real shapes, never glyphs
donts: Don't imitate materials — no gradient brass, no bevels, no embossing
Don't reintroduce card containers, project grids, or scroll-triggered fade-ups
Don't add a second large light field; one bone object per region at most
Don't use monospace; this world stamps and engraves
Don't state anything the product record does not confirm
